cells.tense: You're standing in the open stretch before anything's been pinned down, and your hand on the choice is steady.
cells.ask: Share one half-formed direction with someone and stay in it a week without changing it. It hands you back what it's like to be in a thing instead of circling it.
cells.core:
Nothing's been decided yet and you're not rushing it. You walk through your day letting possibilities go by without grabbing or closing them out, and the ones that matter come forward because they hold when you test them, not because you argued them into place.

What you take on keeps through the week. When an option doesn't survive contact with ordinary days, you drop it without ceremony, and the ones that stay, stay because you're actually in them. What you decide now gets to feed what comes next — the next step shows up already shaped by a choice that stuck.
cells.sheetLine: You decide by trying the thing, not by thinking it through twice.
cells.verb: Two streams meeting and choosing to run as one.
cells.place: The open hour before anything has been settled into a particular form.

cells.tense: You're fixing how it turns out before the two of you have met.
cells.ask: Text one person one plain line about where you are right now, no plan attached. It sets down the shaping long enough for the situation to tell you something.
cells.core:
You pick something up because you want to, and you let the day's shape arrive on its own; the room around you carries marks of what you genuinely chose to tend, one thing at a time, without a picture of the ending pushing you.

Now every direction has been rehearsed against what it'll become. You've imagined who fits and who doesn't, which way this should land, what the ending looks like, and the picture holds more weight for you than the first real exchange. You're steering a version of events that hasn't arrived, and it's crowding out the one that has. That's the cost of shaping a result before anything's happened — you get a tight hold on a picture that's less and less true to what's actually here.
cells.sheetLine: You're deciding how it ends before it's started.
cells.verb: Two streams meeting and choosing to run as one.
cells.place: The open hour before anything has been settled into a particular form.

cells.tense: You don't come near a choice anymore, and it's been a while.
cells.ask: Write down one direction you keep feeling out, what it would actually cost and require, in plain words. It gives you something real to stand next to instead of a torn decision.
cells.core:
You stay with the open state and let it be open — no forced shape, willing to walk through the day and see what comes toward you, and that's how a direction arrives without strain.

When something is possible, you don't fully arrive at it. Better to leave the question blank than pick and be wrong, so you stay around the edges of what you might want and let someone else move first. Nothing gets named and nothing gets feared either. You've been at this doorway since the last time a choice didn't go the way you'd hoped, and the comfort of not deciding has had its way with you.
cells.sheetLine: You'd rather stay undecided than risk being wrong.
cells.verb: Two streams meeting and choosing to run as one.

cells.tense: You're leaning a direction into shape while telling yourself you're only seeing what's there.
cells.ask: Say out loud, once, the direction you'd go if nothing could go wrong. It gives the steering you're doing a name you can stand behind.
cells.core:
You follow what draws you and let the form find itself, and you can say where that pull has led without anyone making you declare it; the attention you give a thing carries the weight of a choice, and you treat it that way in how you talk about it.

What's actually happening is narrower than you say it is. You point your looking one way and then describe it as careful observation. Something draws you and it shows up in your account as evidence. The lean is moving you before you've admitted you're leaning. What hasn't happened yet is you owning that the lean was yours to make.
cells.sheetLine: The pull you're calling your process is you leaning.

attempts.check: The draft says the person picks the form that's theirs and stops re-deciding — nothing in the record says they already know which one, only that choosing happens where things aren't yet fixed. A reader could say the choice isn't theirs to end, that keeping it open is how they stay free. The ask survives either way: putting one rough version in front of someone and holding it seven days works whether or not that version turns out to be the real one. The sentence 'and you can say which one' risks serving the writer's cadence more than the reader, so keep it only if it stays a fact about what picking does, not a compliment.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person is actively steering a direction under the label of open looking — the record only supports misattributed authorship in this seat, not that the person already knows which way they lean. A reader could say they genuinely haven't chosen, that taking in what's there is not the same as deciding. The ask survives being wrong because saying the direction out loud once is information either way. The sheet line 'The pull you're calling your process is you leaning' is the sentence most likely to serve the writer's rhythm over the reader's recognition, so watch that it lands as observation rather than flourish.
